e: President Goïta pardons French national Yann Vezilier, who had been sentenced in June to 20 years in prison over alleged involvement in a plot to destabilise Mali on behalf of the DGSE.
JNIM militants launch an attack on an army garrison in San; 40 militants and 10 soldiers are killed.
More than 50 soldiers and Russian Africa Corps personnel are killed in an ambush by the Azawad Liberation Front and JNIM in the Gao Region.
Mali restores diplomatic relations with Algeria after a yearlong rift, with both countries reinstating ambassadors and reopening their airspace to one another.
The government establishes the Malian Office of Precious Substances, a new state body to regulate and centralise the country's artisanal gold trade.
At least eight civilians are killed in an airstrike on the village of Kyrnia in the Mopti Region that Human Rights Watch attributes to the Russian Africa Corps.
A court sentences French national Yann Vezilier to 20 years' imprisonment, after convicting him over an alleged plot to destabilise the government of President Goïta in 2025.
The government bans the usage of motorcycles with an engine capacity of 125 cc and above outside major urban centres.
At least eight people are killed, and 42 injured, when a civilian passenger bus strikes a land mine on the Bamako–Kayes road near Bamako.
At least 50 people are killed in a JNIM attack on two villages in Mopti Region.
President Goïta assumes the additional role of defence minister following the killing of Sadio Camara in the 2026 Mali offensives.
Former education minister and junta critic Mountaga Tall is abducted by unidentified individuals from his residence in Bamako.
A number of coordinated attacks led by JNIM alongside the Azawad Liberation Front occur in various locations across Mali. Sadio Camara, the minister of defence, is killed during the attacks.
Mali withdraws recognition of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic and endorses the Moroccan autonomy proposal for the Western Sahara.
The United States lifts sanctions on Defense Minister Sadio Camara and two senior military officials over their involvement with the Wagner Group.

The junta arrests Youssouf Sissoko, editor-in-chief of the weekly newspaper L’Alternance, in Bamako on charges of insulting a foreign head of state after publishing an article critical of Nigerien president Abdourahamane Tiani.
At least 15 people are killed in a JNIM attack on a fuel tanker convoy in the west of the country.
The government announces the imposition of nationwide fuel rationing in response to the blockade of supplies by jihadists.
The junta appoints Hilaire Bébien Diarra to head a new ministerial-level position in charge of the mining sector and superseding the Ministry of Mines.
Several people are abducted in a jihadist attack on three industrial sites in Kayes Region.
A ferry sinks after hitting rocks along the Niger River in Diré, Tombouctou Region, killing at least 38 people.
Seven employees are taken hostage in a jihadist attack on the Morila Gold Mine in Sikasso Region; all hostages are released the following evening.
